what_makes_it_best: Takes listings straight from employer and career-site pages, and the job card lets you pick which job site to apply through, so one job shows several apply routes. Sourcing benchmark only: the help page does not say Google merges duplicates.
avoid: none found

what_makes_it_best: Scrapes LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor, ZipRecruiter, Bayt, Naukri, BDJobs and HelloWork concurrently into one dataframe, with an hours_old filter for "new since last run" (exact on Indeed and LinkedIn; Glassdoor rounds up to whole days). Sourcing benchmark only: the README does not mention deduplication.
avoid: LinkedIn returns 429s on bursts, Glassdoor rate-limits above about 2 requests per second, most boards cap near 1000 jobs per search, and the FAQ calls the boards "aggressive with blocking". Plan for retries and fallbacks, not guaranteed coverage.

what_makes_it_best: Groups items from different feeds that cover the same event (normalized-title fuzzy matching plus Elasticsearch more_like_this), shows the highest-scoring copy and lists the other versions beneath as alternate sources, so nothing is silently dropped. Has a user toggle and optional "mark duplicates read".
avoid: Full clustering is gated behind Premium Archive; free users get clusters only on popular feeds. Do not paywall core dedupe.

what_makes_it_best: Compares article text rather than URL, treats items with over 85% overlap as duplicates across different sources only (not within one source), looks back 31 days, and auto-marks a later duplicate as read if the original was already read.
avoid: Does not run in third-party apps that use Feedly as a sync backend, so results differ by client. Apply seen-and-skip consistently everywhere.

what_makes_it_best: Runs a daily plus on-create comparison across up to nine properties, lets you set ordered merge-winner rules (up to five criteria, a tie-breaker, property overrides), and lets you undo a rejected duplicate pair for 14 days.
avoid: Merges are permanent ("Merged records cannot be reverted"), so bulk-merging unchecked can destroy data. Keep a log and a way to undo.

what_makes_it_best: Uses semantic LLM scoring weighted by importance (qualifications about 1/3 to 1/2 of the score, must-haves weighted most, keywords under 20%) and shows a Covered / Not Covered list citing the resume lines behind each item, so matching every keyword still scores low without the qualifications.
avoid: none found (exact weights are not published, and its coarse Poor to Great bands give less ranking resolution than a 0-100 score)

what_makes_it_best: Separates explicit skills (listed on your profile) from implicit skills (extracted from your summary, job descriptions, title and headline) and shows "x of y" required skills matched.
avoid: none found

what_makes_it_best: Keeps Fit and Engagement as separate scores built from capped score groups with an overall cap and optional time decay, and combines them in an A1 to C3 grid (letter = fit, number = engagement); you can test records and preview the score distribution before turning a score on.
avoid: none found. The AI-score variant needs Marketing Hub Enterprise and at least 50 contacts split between converted and not converted; the page describes no per-score explanation feature, so keep your reasons visible.

what_makes_it_best: Defines the field's de facto schema: required datePosted, description, hiringOrganization, jobLocation, title; validThrough for expiry; jobLocationType for 100% remote; applicantLocationRequirements; baseSalary only as the employer gave it. States that expired jobs must be expired (past validThrough, 404/410, or markup removed) or the site risks a manual action.
avoid: Do not infer pay and call it posted pay (Google requires employer-provided baseSalary, never an estimate). Many pages omit validThrough, so no expiry date does not mean open.

benchmark: Google Merchant Center automatic item updates
what_makes_it_best: Treats the landing page as the source of truth: reads schema.org markup for price/availability/condition first, falls back to ML extractors if markup is missing or wrong, then corrects the record or disapproves it when it cannot determine the value. Stops auto-updating if mismatches become too numerous.
avoid: Its stated limits show where extraction is unreliable (pages with multiple strikethrough prices, values that change more than once a day). Do not auto-act on ambiguous pages; route them to a fallback or log them.

benchmark: Simplify Copilot (Tailor Resume, Generate Cover Letter)
what_makes_it_best: Tailoring opens a job-specific resume version where you review each proposed change and apply only the ones you want, so nothing the model suggests lands in the resume unreviewed. Best verified, not proven best: no job tool found documents a no-invented-claims check.
avoid: Docs state no guardrail against invented skills, only tell the user to review; the same page says Autopilot submits with no review step; the essay page says "Do not use a generated achievement or claim that is not accurate", leaving the check to the user.

what_makes_it_best: The API parses citations itself and extracts cited_text from the supplied documents, so every citation is guaranteed to point to a valid span in the source. That is a mechanical version of a claim linter and beats asking the model in a prompt to quote.
avoid: none found

what_makes_it_best: Separate "continuously autofill multipage forms" switch and per-group toggles (contact, documents, education, experience, demographics, work authorization); its docs say "Application filled" is not the employer's submission confirmation, which matches this project's "no confirmation means not sent" rule. No verified benchmark exists for detecting and stopping at a bot check.
avoid: Hands-off Autopilot is a separate mode that submits without review. Unsupported forms fall back to manual copying; a Chrome Web Store reviewer says custom questions and some company portals still need manual input.

what_makes_it_best: Treats an iframe as trusted only if its src matches the saved site (URI match detection); page-load autofill silently skips untrusted iframes, a manual trigger shows a warning, and page-load autofill is off by default because a hostile page could steal credentials. A model for filling cross-host embedded forms on unfamiliar sites.
avoid: none found

benchmark: Simplify Copilot saved answers and field toggles
what_makes_it_best: Saves answers you write and reuses them, warns that even an exact-wording match "does not guarantee the old answer still fits" (old company names, dates), and lets work-authorization and demographic answers be switched off separately. Reuse works only on identical wording, so this project's concept-level reuse (concept_of) goes beyond it.
avoid: LazyApply Trustpilot reviewers (2.1/5, 110 reviews, unverified) report "yes" selected by default on visa and veteran questions: never default eligibility answers (https://www.trustpilot.com/review/lazyapply.com). Simplify's docs tell users to review every generated answer; there is no automated fabrication check.

what_makes_it_best: A fixed vocabulary of field-purpose tokens (given-name, email, tel, organization-title, bday, sex and others) maps a field to stored data without depending on label wording: the right model for reusing one stored fact across differently worded questions.
avoid: none found. Caveat: MDN lists no tokens for work authorization or salary, so those need the project's own concept map.

what_makes_it_best: Separate on/off control per data type, with device re-authentication before sensitive personal data is filled by default: a model for gating a standing-answer bank by category.
avoid: none found

what_makes_it_best: Offers a code only when the site or app in use matches the DNS domain written in the message's last line ("@example.com #123456"), so a code is never placed into a look-alike site. Covers SMS codes; the Mail-app behavior was not confirmed. No job-search tool documents reading emailed codes (no in-field benchmark).
avoid: none found

job: Track and reconcile with the inbox
what_makes_it_best: Matches recruiting mail to each tracked application (an Emails tab per job) and, on an interview invite or rejection, proposes the status change for you to approve, decline or approve-all rather than overwriting the tracker silently.
avoid: Public beta, by request only. The page does not say access is read-only, and the Emails tab lets you send mail. Not every message will match a job. Disconnecting Gmail does not turn off Autopilot's separate email proxy.

job: Track and reconcile with the inbox
what_makes_it_best: Builds and updates one itinerary from forwarded confirmation emails, matches on the sender address, folds overlapping bookings into the existing trip, and sends mail it cannot parse to an "Unfiled Items" bucket instead of dropping it.
avoid: Forwarding from an address not tied to your account silently creates a new account for that address, splitting your data. Mail sent straight from the booking site will not link.

what_makes_it_best: Collects every trigger for a recipient into one notification (optionally one per batch key) over a fixed or sliding window; a sliding window has a required max-extension cap, the batch can close early on a maximum activity count, and the message carries the full total_activities count while rendering only the first or last ten.
avoid: Only ten items render by default and payload strings truncate at 256 characters, so a digest can look complete while hiding items. Always show the total count and a link to the full list.

what_makes_it_best: Each saved search chooses daily or weekly delivery and email, in-app, or both, so new jobs arrive as one digest per alert rather than one ping per posting.
avoid: New alerts default to email plus in-app together (a double ping). Capped at 20 active alerts per member.

what_makes_it_best: Posts an "Inflated Reviews" alert on an employer's profile when it detects the employer artificially boosting its ratings, and removes all contributions tied to an account that breaks the rules (incentivized reviews, proof-of-submission demands, ballot-box stuffing).
avoid: Glassdoor says it cannot fully verify identity, truthfulness or employment status (only "Company Bowls" require a work email) and does not fact-check statements: treat scores as unverified signals, never as verified fact.

what_makes_it_best: Per-company pages with exact offices, employees affected, notice date and layoff date, built from state-filed WARN records rather than crowdsourced reports, and it states which layoffs it misses.
avoid: It does not capture all layoffs (not every state has a WARN act; filing timing varies), so a clean result must not be read as "no layoffs".

what_makes_it_best: Gates full access on verifying a work email by emailed code, so company-specific posts come from people who passed that check. Partly sourced: the page shows the code flow but not what verification unlocks.
avoid: Employers can block Blind's verification emails, locking existing users out (help center names blindapp@teamblind.com as the fallback). Treat missing verification as unknown, not negative.

what_makes_it_best: Transcribes spoken answers in real time and shows, per answer, the job-related terms used, the most-repeated words and the talking points covered, without grading, with unlimited retries on questions written by industry experts. Status unconfirmed: a search snippet suggested the tool is archived. Blog dated June 2022.
avoid: Dice's review found it leans generalist and cannot tie your skills to a specific employer's problems; a tool that must tie talking points to the role needs to add that.

what_makes_it_best: Builds a roleplay by pulling a linked page such as a job description, product page or company overview into the AI's context, so the simulated interviewer reacts to the actual role; also gives feedback on structure, clarity, conciseness, pacing and filler words.
avoid: The link must be publicly accessible (no login) and file pre-reads are Enterprise-only, so fall back to pasted summaries when a posting is behind a login.

what_makes_it_best: Shows a funnel of jobs saved, applications, interviews and offers for a chosen date range, with conversion percentages (applications needed per interview). Field baseline only: the page mentions no breakdown by source, resume version or touchpoint and no sample-size caveat.
avoid: none found

what_makes_it_best: Adjusts p-values and widens each confidence interval for every early look, with the widening shrinking as data accumulates, and warns that early decisions often produce underpowered lift estimates, so early results can be read without declaring a winner on a small sample.
avoid: The docs set no minimum sample or duration, so the tool must define its own floor (CLAUDE.md's 100+ graded applications and 10+ positive replies).

what_makes_it_best: Lets you pick one or more attribution models (First Touch, Last Touch, Linear, Time Decay, Empirical) in one report; the Empirical model weights rarer interaction types more heavily using historical interaction data, so rare high-intent touches count for more than frequent low-intent ones.
avoid: The page states no minimum sample size for the Empirical model. Do not copy a model that outputs credit percentages without a sample-size warning.
